title: iPhone Duo Hinge Fails After 3 Weeks and 400,000 Folds, CNET Reports
body:
Apple’s much‑anticipated iPhone Duo has finally shown its first serious sign of wear after an intensive durability test that pushed the device through more than 400,000 folding cycles in just three weeks. The experiment, conducted by a leading tech‑review outlet using a purpose‑built “Fold‑a‑Phone” rig that folds the handset continuously, revealed that the hinge – the mechanical heart of the foldable design – is beginning to loosen, producing a faint but perceptible wobble. While the phone remains functional, the early failure raises questions about the long‑term reliability of Apple’s entry into the foldable market and could influence consumer confidence as the device prepares for a global launch later this year.

The test rig was engineered to simulate the worst‑case scenario for a foldable smartphone: a nonstop folding motion at a rate of roughly one fold per second, 24 hours a day, for twenty‑nine days. By the end of the trial, the iPhone Duo had completed 416,000 folds, a figure that far exceeds the typical daily usage of even the most avid multitaskers. The rig’s sensors logged the exact moment the hinge’s resistance began to drop, marking the first measurable degradation in the device’s structural integrity. Although the screen and internal components remained intact, the hinge’s emerging play suggests that the mechanical tolerances may be tighter than initially projected.

Apple’s venture into foldables represents a strategic pivot for the company, which has historically prioritized premium materials and meticulous engineering to differentiate its products. The iPhone Duo’s hinge is a departure from the traditional clamshell or sliding mechanisms seen in competing devices, employing a patented “dual‑axis” swivel that promises a seamless transition between tablet and phone modes. Industry analysts had expected Apple to leverage its expertise in precision manufacturing to deliver a hinge that could endure at least a million folds, a benchmark set by some Android rivals. The early onset of wobble, therefore, could be perceived as a shortfall in meeting those durability expectations, especially given the premium price point that Apple is likely to command.

Consumer sentiment around foldable phones has been mixed since their introduction, with early adopters praising the expanded screen real estate while critics point to fragility, bulk, and high cost. The iPhone Duo’s performance in this stress test may amplify those concerns, prompting potential buyers to weigh the novelty of a foldable iPhone against the risk of premature wear. However, it is worth noting that laboratory conditions are far harsher than everyday use; most users will fold their devices far less frequently, and the hinge’s slight looseness may not translate into a noticeable issue in typical scenarios. Moreover, Apple’s reputation for post‑launch software updates and hardware refinements could see a revised hinge design or firmware‑level compensation in future production runs.

From a market perspective, the findings arrive at a pivotal moment as the foldable segment is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate of over 20% through 2030. Competitors such as Samsung, Huawei, and Motorola have already shipped multiple generations of foldables, gradually improving hinge durability and reducing crease visibility. Apple’s entry could accelerate innovation across the board, pushing rivals to further refine their mechanisms. Conversely, if the iPhone Duo’s hinge issues persist in real‑world usage, it may give competitors an edge, reinforcing the narrative that Apple’s foray into this niche is still a work in progress.

Looking ahead, Apple is expected to address the hinge’s early wear in the final production models, potentially incorporating stronger alloys, revised spring dynamics, or additional reinforcement layers. The company’s extensive supply‑chain resources and experience with precision components suggest that a solution is feasible before the device reaches retail shelves. For consumers, the key takeaway is that while the iPhone Duo’s foldable ambition is impressive, durability remains a critical factor that will shape adoption rates. As the launch date approaches, further independent testing and user feedback will be essential to determine whether Apple can deliver a foldable that lives up to its brand promise of lasting quality and seamless user experience.
